description: Single line plot, labelled (b), the second panel of a two-panel simulation figure (panel (a), at T = 950 °C with strain-rate change, is not present in this image group). Axes: x = True strain (linear, ticks 0.1–0.9), y = DRX fraction (linear, 0.0–1.0). Top-left annotations read 'Strain rate:0.01s⁻¹' and 'Model1'. Four sigmoidal DRX-fraction curves are plotted, keyed by a legend at right-centre: solid purple '950°C(Constant)', solid black '1050°C(Constant)', dashed magenta '950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)' and dashed blue '950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)'. The black 1050 °C constant curve is leftmost and steepest, approaching DRX fraction ~1.0 by true strain ~0.6; the purple 950 °C constant curve rises later. The two dashed transient curves (temperature step 950 → 1050 °C imposed at first-stage strain 0.2 or 0.4) lie only marginally above the purple constant curve at the same strain and essentially track its growth, so transiently changing Z_p barely alters the DRX growth rate. Filled circles mark the first-stage strain levels: magenta dots labelled '0.2 strain' and '0.3 strain', blue dots labelled '0.4 strain' and '0.5 strain'. The panel therefore supports Model 1's claim that the second-stage DRX growth rate is set only by the second-stage Z_p.

observations.observation: Panel (b) plots DRX fraction (y, 0.0–1.0) against True strain (x, labelled ticks 0.1–0.9) for a simulation labelled 'Model1' at 'Strain rate:0.01s⁻¹'.
Four curves are shown in the legend: 950°C(Constant) in solid purple, 1050°C(Constant) in solid black, 950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain) in dashed magenta, and 950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain) in dashed blue.
The solid black 1050°C(Constant) curve is the leftmost and steepest, reaching a DRX fraction close to 1.0 near a true strain of 0.6, i.e. it rises well before the other curves.
The dashed 950°C-1050°C transient curves (0.2 strain and 0.4 strain) lie only slightly above the solid purple 950°C(Constant) curve at the same true strain and closely follow its growth rate.
Filled circle markers on the curves are annotated '0.2 strain' and '0.3 strain' (magenta) and '0.4 strain' and '0.5 strain' (blue).
The caption states that panel (b) corresponds to a constant strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹ with T_I = 950 °C and T_II = 1050 °C and first-stage strain ε_I = 0.2 or 0.4.

The caption states that panel (a) of the same figure corresponds to T = 950 °C with strain rates ε̇_I = 0.1 s⁻¹ and ε̇_II = 0.01 s⁻¹ and ε_I = 0.2 or 0.4; that panel is not included in this image group.

The citing text states that the growth rate of the DRX fraction after suddenly decreasing Z_p was identical to the corresponding result under the constant condition in Fig. 15 — consistent with the near-overlap of the dashed transient curves with the purple constant curve seen here.
The citing text explains that in Model 1, t_0.5 was calculated from Eq. (10) and mainly affected by Z_p, so the second-stage DRX kinetics depend only on the temperature and strain rate of that stage.
No numeric values of DRX fraction are printed on the curves; only the strain-level annotations '0.2 strain', '0.3 strain', '0.4 strain' and '0.5 strain' are given as text.

subfigures.description: Line plot of DRX fraction (0.0–1.0) versus True strain (0.1–0.9) for Model 1 at a constant strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹. Four curves: solid purple 950°C(Constant), solid black 1050°C(Constant), dashed magenta 950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain), dashed blue 950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain). Filled circle markers labelled '0.2 strain', '0.3 strain' (magenta) and '0.4 strain', '0.5 strain' (blue) mark first-stage strain levels. The two dashed transient curves sit just above the purple 950 °C constant curve, while the black 1050 °C constant curve rises earliest and most steeply.
